pairs.cause: Inventions like the steam engine powered machines and factories.
pairs.effect: Goods were produced far faster and more cheaply in factories.
pairs.explanation: Machine production replaced slow handmade work, flooding markets with cheaper goods.

pairs.cause: Factory jobs were concentrated in cities.
pairs.effect: People migrated from farms to cities in huge numbers (urbanization).
pairs.explanation: Work moved to the factories, so workers moved to the cities that held them.

pairs.cause: Early factories had long hours, low pay, and dangerous conditions.
pairs.effect: Workers organized labor unions to demand reforms.
pairs.explanation: Harsh conditions pushed workers to unite and bargain for better treatment.

pairs.cause: Factories burned coal and dumped waste.
pairs.effect: Air and water pollution increased sharply in industrial cities.
pairs.explanation: Rapid, unregulated industry damaged the environment and public health.

pairs.cause: Industry created constant demand for raw materials and new markets.
pairs.effect: Industrial nations expanded imperial control over other lands.
pairs.explanation: The hunger for resources and buyers fueled a new wave of imperialism.

pairs.cause: New wealth created factory owners and a larger middle class.
pairs.effect: Society shifted away from being dominated by land-owning nobles.
pairs.explanation: Industrial money created new powerful classes, reshaping the social order.

pairs.cause: Railroads and steamships moved goods and people quickly.
pairs.effect: Trade and communication over long distances expanded.
pairs.explanation: Faster transport knit regions and economies more tightly together.
